members.name: banknifty_lead_lag_v1
members.thesis: Bank NIFTY leads NIFTY 50 by 1-5 minutes during directional moves because banking stocks are the highest-weight sector and institutional flows hit banks first. When Bank NIFTY makes a sharp move but NIFTY laggards haven't caught up, there's a window to trade the laggards. The inefficiency exists due
filters: no trades in first 10 min or last 15 min
trade in direction of Bank NIFTY move only
weaknesses: Lead-lag relationships are not stable — the 'leader' changes based on what's driving the market that day. Bank NIFTY doesn't always lead.
Small per-trade edge (20 bps) with high frequency means costs eat a huge chunk. Any slippage increase destroys profitability.
The 1-5 minute window is extremely tight for Zerodha execution. Co-location traders with DMA will eat this edge before retail can act.
members.prior_art: Lead-lag pairs trading. See: Algorithmic Trading (Chan), Advances in Financial Machine Learning (de Prado) on lead-lag estimation.

members.name: nifty_bank_lag_arbitrage
members.thesis: Exploits lead-lag relationships. Nifty Bank Index futures often lead major constituents (HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank) by 2-5 minutes during sharp moves. Institutional high-frequency traders focus on the index first, then the components. We capture the catch-up move in the component.
weaknesses: Crowding from HFT firms in these liquid names
